chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), that he said:

Feed your sick ones the chard (silq), meaning its leaves, for therein is a healing, and there is no cure with it, nor is there a suffering for it, and it calms the sleep of the patient, and avoid its root for it agitates the black bile.

key_terms.السَّوَاء: Black bile (one of the four humors)
key_terms.السِّلْق: Chard or leafy beet, a type of vegetable

ai.seo_question: What are the medicinal benefits of chard according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him) prescribes chard leaves as a therapeutic remedy for the sick, highlighting their ability to induce restful sleep and promote healing without adverse effects. He specifically advises avoiding the root, noting its tendency to aggravate 'black bile' (sauda), reflecting the Shia scholarly tradition's integration of humoral medicine (tibb) with spiritual and physical well-being. This guidance underscores the practical application of prophetic medicine in maintaining balance within the body's humors.
